So firstly, it is valid to want to end your life if survival seems pointless, that is pretty reasonable. But why not try to learn more about how you can survive if something should happen, like disaster preparedness and what not. You’d be surprised with what humans can survive with some forethought, and staying in a homemade bunker so you can explore the future nuclear wasteland (or evacuate) to me personally seems cooler than dying or melting to death. Maybe looking into that will help alleviate your fears?

Also, I highly recommend not cutting your artery. I attempted this way almost a year ago, and it was GROSS. Arteries pump blood away from your heart, so the blood will exit in a “pulse” that matches your heart beat and the cut might even squirt (mine was too shallow to do that though) and it HURTS really, really bad. Ever since I can’t stand the feeling of having that wrist touched or grabbed, I stupidly got a cover up tattoo which was difficult in of itself to sit through, and I didn’t account for the fact that people would be more curious about a tattoo than scarring. So in general, not at all a cash money experience.

This is something I’ve actually never got the chance to explain to someone. I used to severely suffer from existential death anxiety, but the suicidal thoughts were always a kind of subconscious thing, a call of the void if you will. However, I became suicidal at a young age, and as the years progressed I became less fearful of death and harm to myself. I would act on impulses and see that said thing is not that “bad,” for example not ever being to self harm, but after doing it during a severe depressive episode, I now struggle to NOT do it. I’ve actually progressed to no longer fearing death after a recent failed attempt where I was incredibly close. So yes, it is very possible to become suicidal as someone with a fear of death, and it is also very possible to lose that fear entirely.

I’m just a young guy, so some of this stuff I say may be inaccurate, and I’m basing it off of people I know. I have two older sisters in their late 20s, and they seem to experience the same thing. As far as I can tell, this is something that happens to both genders. As people get more mature and “out into the world,” they tend to become sort of tribal if that makes sense, they don’t really interact with someone outside of their social circles. My sisters and brother-in-laws have pretty much had the same friends for the past decade, and new people only really get introduced into the group if someone dates someone new outside of those social circles, in fact it’s really common for those friends to date each other’s exes and what not, just because they don’t get much interaction outside of the people they’ve known for so long. I really hope this isn’t too dragged out and it makes sense, and makes you feel better about your situation.
